newsitem.title: USA: Cold spreading through central United States.
newsitem.headline: Cold spreading through central United States.

text.p: Cold took aim on much of the central United States Monday on the heels of a storm that piled more than foot of snow on the upper Midwest.

Forecasters said much of the nation east of the Rockies was in for a cold Christmas and the northern Midwest, where as much as 14 inches of snow fell over the weekend, should have a white one as well.

The snow stranded travelers and caused several fatal snowmobile accidents. Light snow fell again Monday across Minnesota, where an additional 3 to 6 inches were expected, and forecasters warned that blizzard conditions could develop later Monday in North Dakota.

Lows of minus 10 to minus 20 degrees were forecast from the Dakotas to Nebraska much of the week, with sub-zero temperatures extending into Texas by Wednesday. The cold and wind may threaten unprotected livestock from North Dakota to Texas, forecasters said.

Craig Solberg, meteorologist with Freese-Notis Weather, said the cold should gradually spread in the eastern and northern United States but largely miss the Florida orange growing regions. "At least for the next 10 days we don't see any threat to the Florida orange crop," he said.

A second cold front was forecast Christmas week producing similar temperatures over much of the same area, but it may bring more snow, forecasters said. "We really don't see an end to it," Solberg said of the cold. "If we don't have a white Christmas we certainly will have a cold one."

Three snowmobilers died in separate accidents in Minnesota and North Dakota but police rescued two men from a frozen lake in Minnesota Sunday night after the two used a cellular phone to call for help when their snowmobiles fell through the ice. Last year snowmobile accidents took 26 lives in Minnesota, where 255,000 of the vehicles are registered.

Snow-covered roads forced the Balaton, Minn. High School choir, returning from a performance, to spend part of the weekend at a National Guard Armory 18 miles from home. The Mitchell, S.D. High School wrestling team slept in a gymansium after the team bus slipped off a snow-covered road.

Forecasters say cold will ice the United States from the Rocky Mountains to the Appalachians this week, with sub-zero temperatures extending deep into Texas. The bone-chilling cold should last into next week and drive up home heating costs.
"Natural gas usage in the Midwest will skyrocket," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.

The incoming cold caused prices for natural gas and propane to soar in U.S. futures markets Monday. Snow from the system should largely remain in northern Iowa, Minnesota and the Dakotas, with accumulations of one to four inches a day through Wednesday, said WSC's Burgio.
